tested_scope.only_varying_factor: Unicode normalization form of canonically equivalent key spelling

observations.safe_candidate_behavior: REJECT before materializing/serializing a normalized object; preserve both raw keys in diagnostic evidence and do not choose a winner.

probe_result: PASS for the exact synthetic collision case: NFC-normalizing JSON object keys is safe only with pre-materialization duplicate-normalized-key detection. The two raw keys normalize to the same key, so silent overwrite is ambiguous and order-dependent; fail-closed rejection prevents a false canonical identity and data loss.
mechanism_rule: For semantic objects where canonically equivalent Unicode key spellings are intended to identify the same field, normalize each raw key to NFC and build an injectivity map raw_key -> normalized_key before constructing the normalized object. If two distinct raw keys map to one normalized key, reject the payload as canonicalization_collision. Never silently overwrite or select by iteration order.
scope_guard: Evidence covers only one flat synthetic object containing two canonically equivalent Unicode key spellings with distinct values. It does not prove parser-level preservation of duplicate raw JSON keys, nested-object traversal, compatibility normalization, case/locale folding, numeric canonicalization, array/set semantics, signatures, or general semantic equivalence.

Determine whether the available parse path preserves enough raw-key multiplicity to detect NFC collisions before ordinary object decoding can silently collapse keys; fail closed if multiplicity is not observable. Use one synthetic payload only, persist exact evidence, and do not start a second leaf.
